groups.title: About your company
groups.note: Asked once and put into every document. Leave anything you do not know yet; it stays yellow.

groups.title: Your choices
groups.note: The usual answers are already filled in. Change any that are not what you do: the policies must match what really happens, because the auditor tests what they say.

shared.name: company
shared.label: Company name

shared.name: system_name
shared.label: The service your SOC report covers
shared.hint: As customers know it, for example Acme Payroll Cloud.

shared.name: security_owner
shared.label: Who owns security (job title)
shared.hint: For example Head of Security or CTO. Owns these documents unless Policies says otherwise.

shared.name: approver
shared.label: Who approves the policies (job title)
shared.hint: Usually the CEO, or the board.

shared.name: security_contact
shared.label: Where people report security problems
shared.hint: An email address or channel, for example security@acme.com.

shared.name: hosting_provider
shared.label: Where the system is hosted
shared.hint: For example AWS eu-west-1, or Microsoft Azure UK South.

shared.name: doc_classification
shared.label: Classification printed on each document

shared.name: review_cycle
shared.label: How often policies are reviewed

shared.name: access_review
shared.label: How often user access is reviewed

shared.name: deprovision_time
shared.label: How soon a leaver's access is removed

shared.name: patch_critical
shared.label: Time to fix a critical vulnerability

shared.name: patch_high
shared.label: Time to fix a high vulnerability

shared.name: backup_frequency
shared.label: How often production data is backed up

shared.name: rto
shared.label: Recovery time objective
shared.hint: How long the service may be down after a disaster.

shared.name: rpo
shared.label: Recovery point objective
shared.hint: How much data, in time, you can afford to lose.

shared.name: training_cycle
shared.label: How often everyone repeats security training

shared.name: vendor_review
shared.label: How often critical vendors are reviewed

shared.name: log_retention
shared.label: How long security logs are kept

shared.name: customer_notice
shared.label: How soon affected customers are told of a breach

shared.name: data_after_contract
shared.label: How soon customer data is deleted after a contract ends

00.b1.label: What does the service do, and for whom?
00.b1.hint: Two or three sentences a customer would recognise.

sys.boundaries.label: The system and its boundaries
sys.boundaries.hint: Taken from Scope. Type here to use different wording.

sys.commitments.label: Service commitments and system requirements
sys.commitments.hint: Taken from Scope. Type here to use different wording.

00.b2.label: Which teams run the system?
00.b2.hint: For example engineering, operations, customer support.
00.b2.context: The <approver role> has overall responsibility. The <security owner role> runs the security programme. ...

01.b1.label: Which process handles breaches of policy?
01.b1.hint: For example 'the disciplinary procedure in the Employee Handbook'.
01.b1.default: the disciplinary procedure in the Employee Handbook
01.b1.context: Breaking this policy may lead to disciplinary action, up to and including dismissal, under ....

documents.title: Code of Conduct and Acceptable Use Policy

02.b1.label: Gift limit
02.b1.hint: The value above which a gift must be declined or declared.
02.b1.context: Never offer or accept bribes, or gifts above ....

02.b2.label: Anonymous reporting channel
02.b2.hint: Where someone can raise a concern without giving their name.
02.b2.context: Speak up about wrongdoing through <security contact> or ..., without fear of retaliation.

03.b1.label: Which identity provider do people sign in with?
03.b1.hint: For example Okta, Google Workspace or Microsoft Entra ID.
03.b1.context: Sign-in to company systems goes through ... with multi-factor authentication.

03.b2.label: Minimum password length
03.b2.context: Passwords are at least ... characters and are kept in the company password manager.

03.b3.label: How do administrators reach production?
03.b3.hint: For example 'the VPN', 'AWS SSO' or 'the bastion host'.
03.b3.context: Production systems are reached only through ....

04.b1.label: Where are changes tracked?
04.b1.hint: For example Jira, Linear or GitHub Issues.
04.b1.context: Every change is tracked in ... and linked to its code or configuration.

04.b2.label: Where is code kept?
04.b2.context: Code is kept in .... Changes reach the main branch only through a pull request reviewed by someone other than the author.

04.b3.label: How soon is an emergency change reviewed?
04.b3.context: A change needed to restore service or fix a serious vulnerability may be released before review. It is reviewed and approved within ... and recorded as an emergency change.

05.b1.label: Where are encryption keys kept?
05.b1.hint: For example AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault.
05.b1.context: Customer data is encrypted at rest. Keys are kept in ... and access to them is restricted.

05.b2.label: How often are vulnerability scans run?
05.b2.context: Systems and code dependencies are scanned for vulnerabilities at least ....

05.b3.label: Where are logs collected?
05.b3.hint: For example Datadog, Splunk or CloudWatch.
05.b3.context: Security-relevant logs from in-scope systems are collected in ... and kept for <log retention>.

06.b1.label: How is someone reached out of hours?
06.b1.hint: For example 'the on-call rota in PagerDuty'.
06.b1.context: Anyone who suspects a security incident reports it to <security contact> immediately. Out of hours, page ....

06.b2.label: How soon must a critical incident get a response?
06.b2.context: Critical | Customer data exposed, or the service down for all customers | ...

documents.title: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan

07.b1.label: What availability do you promise customers?

07.b2.label: Where are the recovery runbooks?
07.b2.hint: Somewhere that still works when production is down.
07.b2.context: Recovery runbooks are kept in ..., where the on-call team can reach them during an outage.

08.b1.label: Which score must be treated?
08.b1.hint: Risks at or above this score need a decision.
08.b1.context: Risks scoring ... or more are treated: reduced with controls, transferred, avoided, or formally accepted by the <approver role>.

09.b1.label: How soon must vendors tell you about a breach?
09.b1.context: Contracts with vendors that hold customer data include confidentiality, security, breach notification within ..., and deletion at the end of the contract.

10.b1.label: How long are other business records kept?
10.b1.context: Other records are kept for ... unless the law requires longer.

11.b1.label: How soon must new starters finish training?
11.b1.context: Everyone completes security awareness training within ... of joining and <training frequency> after that.

11.b2.label: How often are phishing simulations run?
11.b2.context: Phishing simulations are run at least ..., and people who click are offered extra training.

12.b1.label: How often are controls sample-tested internally?
12.b1.context: The <security owner role> tests a sample of controls every ... and records each result in Offset Attest.

12.b2.label: Who carries out the independent review?
12.b2.hint: For example an internal auditor, or an outside consultant.
12.b2.context: At least once a year, someone independent of the control owners reviews the programme: .... The review is planned in advance and its results reported to the <approver role>.
